reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate and adds a shared isNonWorkingDay, but the per-occurrence 'off / skip if daily / move otherwise' decision is not centralised and is re-coded in each consumer.

duplication.why: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange carry near-identical skipWeekend/isDaily/move dispatch loops, getNextDate has its own daily branch, and schedule-template recomputes the daily exception as movesWeekend.

placement.why: Date rules sit in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts as the tree does, though the daily-vs-move dispatch leaks into server handlers and the budget template.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedules date logic, the new handler, the type and release notes; parseRecurDate gaining frequency/holidays is needed.

maintainability.why: Each new weekend rule had to be threaded into four places, with ad hoc search bounds (count*4+holidays.length, 3+holidays.length, MAX_WEEKDAY_SEARCH) that a maintainer must keep consistent.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and budget/schedule-template.ts movesWeekend, each decide daily-skip vs move themselves instead of one shared occurrence-adjust function

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange's loop reshapes getUpcomingDates' skipWeekend/isDaily/getDateWithSkippedWeekend branch (continue vs push, different bounds); schedule-template re-expresses the daily exception as a movesWeekend flag

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily special-case branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and createScheduleList re-implement the daily/move dispatch
